newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end up slightly in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end up slightly in slow trade.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign currency B share index erased early losses to end marginally higher in sluggish trade on Tuesday, boosted by institutional demand for recently listed large-capitalisation issues, brokers said.
The B share index inched up 0.58 points or 0.39 percent to end at 149.70, with turnover contracting to HK$57 million from Monday's HK$65 million.

The domestic A share index fell 8.72 points or 1.97 percent to 434.40, ending a brief rally starting from last Friday after heavy losses caused by Beijing's latest move to crack down on over-speculation, brokers said.
Turnover on Tuesday was 6.5 billion yuan against 8.1 billion yuan on Monday.
"Institutional demand for newly-listed B shares lifted the B share index despite the poor performance of cheap-priced shares," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
"Newcomers, which are mostly large-capitalised and have a solid earnings record, are likely to remain the target of buying for some time," the analyst said.
On the B share market, newcomer Beijing Orient Electronics was the most actively traded on volume of 3.2 million shares, gaining HK$0.12 to HK$4.30.
Recently listed pesticide maker Hubei Sanonda jumped HK$0.08 to HK$4.58 with 1.7 million shares changed hands, making it the day's second most actively traded B shares.
Brokers said B shares would probably fluctuate in a tight band later this week, with the direction of their A share counterparts unclear.
They said the A share market today was driven down by selling from banks as the Friday deadline for them to unwind their equity positions approached.
A share newcomers were among the biggest losers. Large amounts of bank funds, now being forced out of the market, were used to subscribe to new share initial public offerings, brokers said.
"With the ban on state banks and enterprises and listed firms trading shares, the market will have difficulty rising strongly," an analyst with Shenzhen J&A Securities said.
Shenzhen's A share market early this year experienced a bull-run which was stopped dead in its tracks in May by a string of crackdown measures launched by Beijing.
Newcomer chemical concern Beijing Huaer, which debuted on Monday, was the sharpest loser in the A share market on Tuesday. It dropped 1.40 yuan to its 10 percent limit-down level at 12.59 yuan.
